title: Run configuration
description: What a server answers, a signed 200, to a run's registration, the signed POST to its run endpoint, and to a reload by the run's id, the signed GET of the run endpoint followed by a slash and the run id: the server's policy for the run, the image it starts in and the variables the agent's process receives, chosen by the server for the run, by the labels its registration sent. The registration's about never selects or changes a security policy. {"version": 1} is an answer of no policy. The digest the server sends beside it, X-Qory-Run-Configuration, is sha256= and the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes of this document as the server sends it; an attach answer contains the digest of the document a reload of the run answers, without labels and about. A member Forager does not recognise is ignored.

version.description: The document format. Forager refuses a version it does not read.

security_policy.description: The server's policy for the run, a policy document in the same shape as the machine's local policy. The policy the command passes, when there is one, narrows it: the node only takes away. Absent, the node's policy is the run's.

image.description: The image the run starts in, a reference pinned by digest, NAME@sha256: and 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits, which the machine runs only under one of its images.allow prefixes. Any other value is refused, run_configuration_invalid: a value that is no string by the schema, and a string that is no reference pinned by digest, with a tag, in upper case, without a digest or the machine's name for an image, by Forager's check before the schema reads it. The run configuration, the server's policy and the node's policy name the same image wherever two of them name one. Fixed when the run starts. Absent, the run's policy selects the image.

variables.description: The variables the agent's process receives, by name, as the server resolved them among its levels: an object with the value each. The server's value of a name wins over every value the node passes for it; the run's fixed names win over the server's. Forager leaves out a name its deny list matches, whose built-in QORY_* entry leaves in QORY_RUN_SYSTEM and QORY_RUN_REPOSITORIES, the system and the repositories a run's preparation may use, by these names exactly; a name it, the wall, the runtime's preparation, a placeholder or the harness's computed values set; a name the run's runtime declares or reserves; a name a value of the machine's is read from, such as a credential's variable; and, in an unwalled run, every one unless the node accepts them. With an API credential among the run's credentials, Forager sets the runtime's model endpoint variable to its endpoint, and leaves every other value of it out as fixed. Without one, behind a wall, the runtime's denies do not leave out the value of the runtime's model endpoint variable: Forager leaves it out when it is not an https URL with a host Forager reads, or its host is none of the hosts of the run's model credential. A value is at most 4096 bytes of UTF-8 and contains no NUL, carriage return or line feed.

credentials.description: The credentials whose values the server stores for the run, at most 8, each name once, and at most 6 of them API credentials. The order of the key group's API credentials is the order in which the gateway sets them (model_credential). The document has no value: the server seals the values to the access key in its answer, secrets-answer.schema.json, to the secrets request, secrets-request.schema.json, a POST to the configuration's secrets.url. The gateway sends it when the run starts, for every entry, and again for each entry whose value has expires_at: 5 minutes before it expires, and after a host answers 401 to a request that the value was set on, at most every 30 seconds per entry. It sets each value in place of a credential of the machine's that claims one of its hosts. The entries are fixed for the run: a renewal changes only the value.

model_credential.description: The name of the model key the runtime starts with, the start key: an API credential of credentials, or a model key the machine defines and the run's policy selects. Required when the run has two or more model keys, of the server's and the machine's together; with one, that one is the start key. When the start key is an API credential, it and every API credential with its format, auth and endpoint are the key group, in the order of credentials. The gateway holds every model key of the run and sets one key of the group, the active key, on requests to its endpoint's host that contain the start key's placeholder: the start key first, then the next key of the group, by the order of credentials, after a provider's limit refusal. The session gives the runtime the start key's variable and endpoint alone. A name of no model key of the run, or of a credential without format, is run_configuration_invalid. Fixed when the run starts.

stack_hosts.description: The hosts the run's stack proxy allows beside the gateway's gateway.stack_hosts, for qory's fetch of the harness definition before the run's first session joins, such as ["git.example", "api.git.example"]: 1 to 32, none twice, each in the grammar of the policy's egress.allow entries. The node's policy decides each host: a host an entry matches passes only when the node's policy allows it and has no path rule for it, since the stack proxy does not check the node's path rules. Behind a wall or a separate gateway they open no address of the gateway's machine and no private network address: the stack proxy reaches those only for a host that gateway.stack_hosts and the node's policy both list by name. Fixed when the run starts. Absent, the stack proxy allows gateway.stack_hosts alone.

resume.description: The paused run whose runtime session this run continues: the paused run's id, and the runtime's session id and the path of its transcript, as that run's last dev.qory.session.transcript has them. Before the runtime starts, the session reads the transcript over the gateway's link, which reads it from the server with GET /resume/transcript of the run API, writes it at path, and adds the descriptor's resume.args. When the read or the write fails, the session starts the runtime without a resume and writes one dev.qory.run.log line. Fixed when the run starts. Absent, the session starts the runtime without a resume.

run_id.description: The id of the paused run, a lower-case UUID.

session_id.description: The runtime's session id in the paused run, as dev.qory.session.transcript has it.

path.description: The transcript's path, as dev.qory.session.transcript has it: under the runtime's home, such as ~/.claude/projects/-workspace/<session_id>.jsonl, or absolute. It lies under the descriptor's resume.prefix.

runs.description: The paused runs this run continues, oldest first, through each run's continuation, at most the newest 256; the last is run_id. Fixed when the run starts.

harness_hidden.description: Whether the run's harness is one the run's workspace may not see, such as one of another organisation. True: the stack channel's dev.qory.run.egress has no path and no path_rule, and the open's dev.qory.run.policy_applied lists each harness credential by name and purpose alone. Fixed when the run starts. Absent, false.

variable.description: One variable: its value. Forager ignores an attribute it does not recognise; one it must honour needs a new revision.

credential.description: One credential whose value the server stores, with no value: the server seals it to the access key in its answer to the secrets request, secrets-answer.schema.json. An API credential, with format, is a model key, and the session gives it to the runtime's variable for that API format and auth. A host credential, with apply, is any other secret.

api_credential.description: A model key: its name, the API format and endpoint it is for, how its value is set, the paths it is set on, the prefixes a value must start with, and what the gateway needs for its cooldown. The gateway sets the value on the endpoint's host alone, on paths, or on every path without them. The session gives the key to the variable the run's runtime's descriptor lists for the format and auth in model.keys, and sets the runtime's endpoint variable to endpoint, in place of every other value of it. A run whose runtime lists no key for the format, or none with this auth, is run_configuration_invalid.

name.description: The credential's name, unique among the entries.

format.description: The API format the endpoint serves.

endpoint.description: The base URL of the model API, such as https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic.

auth.description: How the value is set on a request, a scheme from the closed set.

paths.description: The paths of the endpoint's host the gateway sets the value on, such as ["/backend-api/codex/*"], in a host credential's grammar. A request to another path of the host gets no value of the key, and passes only as the run's policy allows it. Absent, the gateway sets the value on every path of the host.

key_prefixes.description: The prefixes a value must start with, such as sk-ant-. The gateway refuses a value that starts with none of them when it loads it. Absent, any value is taken.

resets_at.description: The key's earliest reset in a provider's response, as the server had it at the claim, an RFC 3339 time. While no response of the provider in the run has a reset of the key, the gateway takes it as the key's known reset when it chooses the next key after a limit refusal; the server sends the keys in the order that breaks ties, not by it (README §Credentials, Several model keys). Absent when no response had one.

schedule_resets_at.description: The next reset of the key's weekly schedule after the claim, an RFC 3339 time. The gateway sets the key's cooldown to it when a limit refusal has no reset, and to it plus 7 days once it has passed. The gateway also takes it, or it plus 7 days once it has passed, as a known reset of the key when it chooses the next key after a limit refusal (README §Credentials, Several model keys). Absent when the key has no schedule.

pause_for_s.description: The cooldown in seconds when a limit refusal has no reset and the key has no schedule_resets_at, 1 to 604800. The server sends it from the provider's settings or catalogue. Absent, the gateway takes 60 for an API key and 3600 for a subscription, a key whose auth has oauth.

cooldown_until.description: The end of the key's cooldown at the claim, an RFC 3339 time, for a key at its limit, or at its use_up_to_percent, when the server claimed the run. The gateway starts the key in cooldown until then, or until a later state of the key allows it. The start key, model_credential, never has one in the future: such a run configuration is run_configuration_invalid. Absent for a key out of cooldown.

chosen.description: true for the key of the model choice, which the gateway makes active first whenever it is out of cooldown (README §Credentials, Several model keys). Only one key of the key group may have it; two are run_configuration_invalid. Absent for every other key.

use_up_to_percent.description: The key's Use up to percentage, 1 to 99, with use_up_to_windows: runs use the key while the utilization of every window in use_up_to_windows is below it. While a listed window's utilization is at or above it and the window's resets_at is after the gateway's clock, the gateway counts the key in cooldown until that resets_at, the furthest one when several listed windows are at it, and sets the next key of the group (README §Credentials, Several model keys). The gateway stores no cooldown for it: its model keys report has the window as the provider's response has it. A window with no utilization, or with no resets_at after the gateway's clock, does not put the key in cooldown. The server also sends cooldown_until, the window's reset, for a key whose stored utilization is at or above the percentage at the claim. A value outside 1 to 99, and one without use_up_to_windows, are run_configuration_invalid. Absent, runs use the key up to the provider's limit.

use_up_to_windows.description: The limit windows use_up_to_percent applies to, 1 to 11, none twice, each in the grammar of the window of model-keys-report.schema.json, such as ["five_hour", "seven_day"]. The server sends the windows of the provider's catalogue entry, Qory Apiary's limit_windows. A window the gateway does not report never puts the key in cooldown. Present with use_up_to_percent alone; one without it is run_configuration_invalid.

host_credential.description: Any other secret: its name, where and how its value is set, and the variables the enclosure gets a placeholder in.

name.description: The credential's name, unique among the entries.

apply.description: Where and how the value is set: 1 to 16 items. The value in the answer to the secrets request may have narrower items (sealed-plaintext.schema.json); without them the gateway sets these.

placeholders.description: Variables the enclosure gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that needs one set to start. A placeholder goes only into a variable for a credential: one that the run's runtime's descriptor denies, lists in its model overrides or reserves, reads its model endpoint or a model key from is run_configuration_invalid. A harness credential with placeholders is run_configuration_invalid: no session gets it.

purpose.description: What the value is for. work: the run's proxy sets it, for the run's sessions, its host work and its setup. harness: the run's stack proxy sets it, for qory's fetch of the harness definition before the run's first session joins, and the run's proxy never does; the gateway overwrites the value with zeros at the run's first join request. Each host of a harness credential's items must be one the stack proxy allows: in gateway.stack_hosts, or in stack_hosts and allowed by the node's policy with no path rule for it. Two harness credentials may claim one host as two work credentials may; a harness credential and a work credential on one host do not conflict, since no proxy sets both. Absent, work.

apply.description: One way a host credential's value is set: an item of credential.schema.json's apply without token, with exact hosts. Several host credentials may claim one host when each item on it has paths and no path of one overlaps a path of another; the proxy sets the one whose paths match the request, and a request no credential's paths match gets none. An item without paths is alone on its hosts.

hosts.description: The hosts the value is set on, each exact: a DNS name or an IP literal, never a *. pattern.

scheme.description: bearer sets Authorization: Bearer and the value. basic sets Authorization: Basic with username and the value as the password. header sets the header in header to the value.

paths.description: The paths of those hosts the value is set on. Absent means every path.

credential_paths.description: The paths a credential's value is set on, in the policy's path grammar: 1 to 32, none twice, each a path from the root, matched whole, or up to a final * matched as a prefix, such as /backend-api/codex/*. No other wildcard, no query.

endpoint.description: A model API's base URL: https, a host, an optional port and path, and no user information, query or fragment, at most 2048 characters. Forager refuses, run_configuration_invalid, one whose host policy.EndpointHost does not read.

key_prefixes.description: 1 to 4 literal prefixes, each 1 to 32 characters of printable ASCII without a space, none twice.

credential_name.description: A credential's name: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, underscore, dot and dash, starting with a letter or a digit.

credential_host.description: An exact host: a lower-case DNS name whose last label starts with a letter, an IPv4 address of four decimal parts with no leading zero, or an IPv6 address of lower-case hex groups with no leading zero, without brackets or a zone. The server writes an IPv6 address in RFC 5952's form; the pattern does not check which run of zero groups :: replaces.
